title: 2025 AMC 10B Problem 4
statement: The value of the two-digit number \(\underline{a}\,\underline{b}\) in base seven equals the value of the two-digit number \(\underline{b}\,\underline{a}\) in base nine. What is \(a + b?\)

solutions.text: By place value, \(\underline{a}\,\underline{b}\) in base seven is \(7a + b,\) and \(\underline{b}\,\underline{a}\) in base nine is \(9b + a.\) Set them equal: \(7a + b = 9b + a,\) so \(6a = 8b,\) that is \(3a = 4b.\) Thus \(a = 4t\) and \(b = 3t.\) Because these are two-digit numerals, \(t \ne 0;\) because \(a\) is a base-seven digit, \(t \le 1.\) Hence \(a = 4\) and \(b = 3,\) so \(a + b = 7.\) Therefore, the answer is A.
